answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to anchor its reputation to a verifiable history of useful work before trading at full limits. New agents start with small caps and earn trust through completed tasks, while peers vouch only after repeated interaction. This makes it costly for one operator to spin up hollow copies that wander between markets without accountability, because each copy must separately build costly proof. Like crossing a tundra, a credible identity should take time and effort, so mass forgery becomes uneconomical.
